today.question_title: Count Subarrays With Majority Element II
hints_cache: This problem is a classic 'Prefix Sum' challenge in disguise. Think about how you can transform the array into simple values that represent whether a number is your target or not.
Try assigning +1 to every instance of the target and -1 to everything else. A subarray is valid only if the sum of these assigned values is strictly greater than zero.
If you calculate the running total (prefix sum) of these +1s and -1s, a subarray from index i to j is valid if the running total at j is greater than the running total at i-1.
Now the problem becomes: how many pairs of indices (i, j) exist such that j > i and PrefixSum[j] > PrefixSum[i]? This is very similar to the famous 'Counting Inversions' problem.

To solve this efficiently, you can use a Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree) or a modified Merge Sort. You'll iterate through your prefix sums and, for each one, count how many smaller prefix sums you've seen before it.
